farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ﴾: you put kasra on the alif of (أنّ) and on the one after it in its jawāb (apodosis), as a fresh start (iʾtināf), and that is in the reading of the Readers.
And if you wish, you put fatḥa on the alif of (أنّ), meaning: your Lord has written upon Himself that whoever does…
And for the (أنّ) that comes after the fāʾ you have both kasra and fatḥa. As for the one who reads it with fatḥa, he says: the writing (al-kitāb) needs (أنّ) only once; but the predicate (khabar) is its proper place, so when it entered at the beginning of the speech it was repeated in its proper place; as He said: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ﴾: since the position of أنّ is "does he promise you that you will be brought forth when you have died", it entered at the beginning of the speech and at its end. Similar to it is: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنّهُ مَـنْ تَوَلاَّهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ﴾ with fatḥa. And similar to it is: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّهُ مَنْ يُحَادِدِ اللّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَأَنّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾. And you may put kasra on the (إن) that comes after the fāʾ in these passages, as a resumption (istiʾnāf); do you not see that you would find it good to say: "كتب أنه من تولاه فهو يضله" ("It was written that whoever takes him as an ally, he leads him astray") with fatḥa [Translator's note: i.e. with fatḥa on the first أنه]. Likewise "وأصلح فهو غفور رحيم" ("and makes amends, then He is Forgiving, Merciful"), if it were so, it would be correct. So whenever the insertion of (هو) is good, the kasra is good.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِيَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: you put (السبيل) in the nominative by His saying (وليستبين), because the verb belongs to it. Whoever treats السبيل as feminine says: ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾. And the verb may be made to belong to the Prophet ﷺ, so you put السبيل in the accusative, the meaning being: "and that you, O Muhammad, may make clear the way of the criminals (ولتستبين يا محمد سبيلّ المجرمين)".

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلاَّ للَّهِ يَقُصُّ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾: it was written with the yāʾ dropped because it meets the alif and lām [Translator's note: i.e. the reading يقضِ الحقّ, written without yāʾ]; just as ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانيَةَ﴾ was written without wāw, and as ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾ was written without yāʾ, following the pronunciation. This is the reading of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]. And it is reported from ʿAlī that he read: (يَقُصُّ الْحَقَّ) with ṣād. He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, he said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to me from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from a man from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read (يقضِى بالحق). Al-Farrāʾ said: and so it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: it is permissible to put it in the nominative (rafʿ).

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ مَن يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِّن ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً﴾: one says خُفيَة and خِفية. And there is a dialect form of it with wāw — not valid in recitation —: خُفوة and خِفوة; just as it is said: "he untied his ḥubwa (حُبْوته), ḥibwa (حِبوته) and ḥibya (حِبْيته)".
His saying: ﴿لَّئِنْ أَنجَانَا مِنْ هَـٰذِهِ﴾ is the reading of the people of Kufa — and so it is in their codices —: "أن ج ى ن ألف" [Translator's note: i.e. spelled with a yāʾ, nūn and alif: أنجينا]; some of them read with the alif (أنجانا), and the reading of the people at large is (أنجيتنا) with tāʾ.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱلْقَادِرُ عَلَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَاباً﴾: as He did to the people of Noah: the rain, the stones and the flood. ﴿أَوْ مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾: the swallowing up by the earth (al-khasf). ﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً﴾: He mixes you up into factions (shiyaʿ) of differing whims.

farraa:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن ذِكْرَىٰ﴾ is in the position of the accusative or the nominative; [the accusative] by an implied (muḍmar) verb: (ولكِن) we remind them a (ذِكرى) reminding; and the nominative on the reading: (ولكن) it is (ذكرى) a reminder.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿وَذَرِ الَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَهُمْ لَعِباً وَلَهْواً﴾: it is said: there is no people but that they have a feast, and they amuse themselves at their feasts, except the community of Muhammad ﷺ; for their feasts are piety, prayer, takbīr and good.
His saying: ﴿وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أَن تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ﴾ means: [lest a soul] be held in pledge. (The Arabs say: "هذا عليك بَسْل", i.e. this is forbidden to you. And for that reason it is said "أسَد باسل", i.e. a lion that is not to be approached.) And the Arabs say: "أعْطِ الراقِىَ بُسْلته" ("give the charmer his busla"), which is the fee for the charm.

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and his wife were calling their son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān to Islam. That is His saying: ﴿إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾, i.e. obey us. And if it were "إِلى الهدى أن ائتنا" it would be correct; as He said: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحاً إِلَى قَوْمِهِ أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ﴾, in many similar cases, where أَنْ is sometimes brought and sometimes dropped.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاةَ...﴾ is referred back (maʿṭūf) to the lām in His saying: ﴿وأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ﴾. The Arabs say: "أمرتك لتذهب" ("I commanded you that you go"), (and "وأن تذهب"); so أَن is in the position of the accusative by being referred back to the command. And there is much like it in the Qurʾān.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾: it is said that His saying (فيكون) refers specifically to the Trumpet (al-ṣūr), i.e. He says to the Trumpet: (كُنْ فَيَكُونُ).
And it is said that His saying (كن فيكون) belongs with His saying "His word is the truth (هو الحقّ)", as a naʿt (description) of the word; then you make its verb ﴿يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾, meaning: His word will be the truth on that day. And it may be that you say: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾ of every thing, so that it is a self-sufficient phrase, and you put "the word (القول)" in the nominative by "the truth (الحقّ)", and put (اليوم) in the accusative because it is the setting (maḥall) for "His word is the truth".
The Arabs say: نِفخ فى الصورِ and نُفِخَ; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (كهيئة الطير فأنفخها فتكون طيرا بإذنى). And the poet said:
لولا ابنُ جَعْدة لم يُفتَح قُهُنْدُزكم * ولا خُراسانُ حتى يُنْفَخَ الصورُ
(Were it not for Ibn Jaʿda, your citadel would not have been opened, nor Khurāsān, until the Trumpet is blown.)
And it is said that al-ṣūr is a horn; and it is said: it is a plural of ṣūra (form), the blowing into the forms (al-ṣuwar) being into the dead.
And Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾: it is said: آزر is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), and it does not take tanwīn (lā yujrā) because it is foreign (aʿjamī). The genealogists are agreed that he was the son of Tāraḥ, so it is as though Āzar was a nickname for him. And it has reached me that the meaning of (آزر) in their language is "crooked", as though he reproached him for his deviation and crookedness from the truth. Some of them read (لأبيه ازرُ) in the nominative, as a vocative (with يا), and that is a good reading. His saying: ﴿أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَاماً آلِهَةً﴾: you put the idols in the accusative because the verb falls upon them.

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ﴾: one says جنّ عليه الليل and أَجَنَّ, and أَجنَّه الليل and جَنّه الليل; with the alif is better when you drop (على), and it is more common than جنَّه الليل.
Two views are given on His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ رَأَى كَوْكَباً قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّي﴾: that he said "this is my Lord" only to draw his people step by step towards the proof against them, in order to reproach their gods as being nothing, and that the star, the moon and the sun were greater than them and yet were not gods; and it is said: he said it in the other sense; as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَى. وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالاّ فَهَدَى﴾; and here they adduced as proof Abraham's saying: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ يَهْدِنى رَبِّى لأَكُونَنّ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الضَّالِّينَ﴾.

farraa:100-100.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾: if you wish you may make ﴿الجِنّ﴾ an explanation of "partners". And if you wish you may make its accusative be on [the meaning]: they made the jinn partners to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
His saying: ﴿وَخَرَقُواْ﴾: and اخترقوا, خلقوا and اختلقوا, meaning: they fabricated.

farraa:102-102.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾: ﴿خَالِقُ﴾ is put in the nominative as a new start (ibtidāʾ), or as being a khabar (predicate). If you put it in the accusative, since it has no alif and lām, by way of qaṭʿ (cutting off), it would be correct; it is like His saying: ﴿غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ﴾, and likewise: ﴿فَاطِرِ السَّمَوَاتِ والأَرْضِ﴾ — if you put it in the accusative when there is a complete definite noun before it, that would be permissible; for you may say: "الفاطر السموات", "الخالق كل شىء", "القابل التوب", "الشديد العقاب". And you may say: "مررت بعبد الله محدِّثِ زيد" ("I passed by ʿAbd Allāh, the one who talks with Zayd"), making it definite even though alif and lām would fit it well, when he has become known by that; so it is like your saying: "مررت بوحشىّ قاتل حمزة" ("I passed by Waḥshī, the slayer of Ḥamza"), and "بابن ملجَم قاتِل علىّ" ("by Ibn Muljam, the slayer of ʿAlī"): he became known by it until it became like a name for him.

farraa:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسْتَ﴾: they say: you learned from the Jews. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (وليقولوا درس), meaning Muhammad ﷺ. It is as you say in speech: "قالوا لى: أساء" ("they said to me: he did wrong") and "قالوا لى: أسأت" ("…you did wrong"). Similar to it: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَيُغْلَبُونَ﴾ and ﴿سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾.
Some read (دارست), meaning: you disputed with the Jews and they disputed with you; and so said Ibn ʿAbbās. Mujāhid read it (دارَسْت) and explained it: you read to the Jews and they read to you.
And it has been read (دُرِسَتْ), i.e. it was read and recited. And they read (دَرُسَتْ) and they read (دَرَسَتْ), meaning: it has grown old, i.e. this that he recites to us is something that has lasted long and passed by us.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَآ آتَيْنَاهَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾: that is because they said to him: "Do you not fear that our gods will strike you with madness for your reviling them?" So he said to them: "Do you not fear that yourselves from them, since you have made equal the small and the great, the male and the female — that the great one will be angry since you have made the small one equal to it?" Then he said to them: "Is the one who worships one god more entitled to be safe, or the one who worships scattered gods?" They said: "The one who worships one god", and so they became angry with themselves. That is His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَآ آتَيْنَاهَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ﴾: this hāʾ is for Noah: and (We guided) of his offspring David and Solomon. If David and Solomon were put in the nominative on this meaning, since the verb is not overt, it would be correct; just as you say: "أخذت صدقاتِهِم لكل مائة (شاةٍ شاةً) وشاةٌ" ("I took their alms: for every hundred sheep, one sheep"), [with شاة in the accusative] and [in the nominative] شاةٌ.

farraa:86-86.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْيَسَعَ﴾: the companions of ʿAbd Allāh double the lām [Translator's note: i.e. read وَاللَّيْسَع], and that is more like the foreign names than [the reading of] those who say (والْيَسَعَ); the Arabs hardly ever put alif and lām on what does not take tanwīn (mā lā yujrā), such as Yazīd and Yaʿmur, except in poetry; one of them recited:
وَجَدْنا الوليد بن اليزيد مباركا * شديدا بأَحْنَاء الخِلافةِ كاهِله
(We found al-Walīd son of al-Yazīd blessed, his shoulders strong to bear the burdens of the caliphate.)
He put the alif and lām on Yazīd only because he had put them on al-Walīd. And when the Arabs do that, they give the word a touch of praise.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِن يَكْفُرْ بِهَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾ means the people of Mecca; ﴿فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنَا بِهَا قَوْماً﴾ means the people of Medina; ﴿لَّيْسُواْ بِهَا بِكَافِرِينَ﴾ — [disbelieving] in the sign (al-āya).

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾: they did not magnify Him as He truly should be magnified. His saying ﴿تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَرَاطِيسَ﴾: He says: how could you say "Allah has not sent down anything to a human being", when the Torah was sent down to Moses ﴿تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَرَاطِيسَ﴾; and al-qirṭās in this place is a sheet. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَاباً فى قِرْطَاسٍ﴾ means: on a sheet.
﴿تُبْدُونَهَا وَتُخْفُونَ كَثِيراً﴾: He says: you show what you like, and you conceal the description of Muhammad ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾: Muhammad ﷺ was commanded to say ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾, i.e. Allah sent it down to you. And if you wish you may say: say: (He is) Allah.
And His saying ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾ may be an answer to His saying: ﴿مَنْ أَنزَلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِهِ مُوسَىٰ﴾ — ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾ sent it down. I chose putting ﴿ٱللَّهُ﴾ in the nominative not as an answer only because it is Allah, Blessed and Exalted, who commanded Muhammad ﷺ to ask them: ﴿مَنْ أَنزَلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾, and it is not a question from them so that they would be answered; but it is permissible because it is a question, and a question may have an answer.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾: if it were in the jussive (jazm) it would be correct; as He said: ﴿ذَرْهُمْ يأكُلُوا وَيَتَمتّعُوا﴾.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾: it is said in the exegesis that the Mother of Towns (umm al-qurā) is Mecca.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾: the hāʾ may refer to Muhammad ﷺ or to the Revelation.

farraa:93-93.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: it is said that it was revealed concerning Musaylima the Liar, and that is because he claimed prophethood.
﴿وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ﴾: and مَن is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ). He means: and who is more wrongful than this one and than this one who said: "I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down." It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ.
That is because he used to write for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when the Prophet ﷺ said: ﴿وَاللّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمُ﴾ he would write (سميع عليم) or (عزيزحكيم), and the Prophet ﷺ would say to him: "It is the same"; until he dictated to him His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلاَلَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ﴾, and Ibn Abī Sarḥ said ﴿فَتَبَارَكَ اللّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ﴾, in wonder at the detailing of the creation of man. He said: and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Thus was it sent down to me", so he doubted and apostatised. And he said: "If Muhammad ﷺ is truthful, then it has been revealed to me (as it was revealed to him), and if he is lying, then I have said the like of what he said." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down concerning him: ﴿وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنَزلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: and it is said: stretching out their hands to draw out the souls of the disbelievers. It is like His saying: ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ﴾. If it were (باسطون), it would be (أيدِيَهُمْ) [in the accusative]; and if it were "باسطو أيديهم أن أخرِجوا" it would be correct. Similar to it, among cases where أن is left out, is His saying: ﴿يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهدَى ائْتِنَا﴾. And when you drop (أن) from speech like this, a verb of saying is implied (muḍmar) in it, as in His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تـَرَى إِذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — they say: ﴿رَبَّنا﴾.

farraa:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَىٰ﴾: it is a plural. The Arabs say: [a people] فرادى and فرادُ, O you, and they do not give it tanwīn (lā yujrūnahā), likening it to ثُلاَث and رُبَاع. The singular of فرادى is فَرْد, فرِد and فريد; and فراد is for the plural, and فرد is not permissible in this sense. One of them recited to me:
ترى النُعَراتِ الزُرْق تحت لَبَانه * فُرَادَ ومثنى أصعقتها صواهِله
(You see the blue gadflies beneath his breast, singly and in pairs, struck down by his neighing.)
His saying: ﴿لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: Ḥamza and Mujāhid read (بينُكُمْ), meaning "your bond". And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (لقد تقطع ما بينَكم), and that is the natural form of the speech. When the verb is made to belong to بين it is left in the accusative; just as they say: "أتانى دونك من الرجال" ("there came to me men below you"), leaving it in the accusative although it is in the position of the nominative, because it is a description (ṣifa). And when they say: "هذا دون من الرجال" ("this is an inferior one among men") they put it in the nominative in the nominative position. Likewise you say: "بين الرجلين بين بعيد" and "بون بعيد" ("between the two men is a great gap"); when you use it on its own you give it tanwīn in Arabic and give it the case inflection (iʿrāb).

farraa:96-96.t:
His saying: ﴿فَالِقُ ٱلإِصْبَاحِ﴾: al-iṣbāḥ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أصبحنا إصباحا" ("we entered the morning"), and al-aṣbāḥ is the morning of each day, collectively.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلْلَّيْلَ سَكَناً وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ حُسْبَاناً﴾: الليل is in the position of the accusative in meaning. So He referred the sun and the moon back to its meaning, since He separated between them by His saying (سكنا); and when you do not separate them by anything, they prefer the genitive. And the accusative is permissible even if nothing comes between them; one of them recited:
وبينا نحن ننظره أتانا * معلِّقَ شَكْوةٍ وزِنادَ راع
(While we were watching for him, he came to us, hanging up a water-skin and a shepherd's fire-stick.)
And you say: "أنت آخذٌ حقَّك وحَقِّ غيرك" ("you are taking your right and the right of others"), putting the second in a genitive construct while you gave tanwīn to the first; because the meaning of your saying "أنت ضارب زيدا" and "ضاربُ زيدٍ" is the same. The best of this is that you put something between them; as Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فظلّ طُهاة اللحم من بينِ مُنْضِج * صفيفَ شِواءٍ أو قَدِيرٍ معجَّلِ
(And the cooks of the meat kept on, some ripening a row of roast, or a hastened pot-stew.)
So he put الصفيف in the accusative and القَدِير in the genitive, according to what I told you.

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾ means in the womb, ﴿وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾ in the man's loins. And it is read (فمستقِرّ), meaning the child in the womb, (ومستودع) in the man's loins. Its nominative is by implying a description (ṣifa) [Translator's note: i.e. an implied predicate such as "of them"]; as when you say: "رأيت الرجلين عاقل وأحمق" ("I saw the two men: a wise one and a fool"), meaning: of them is such and such.

farraa:109-109.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: those swearing are the disbelievers. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to bring them the sign that was revealed in al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾; so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to have it sent down and swore that they would believe. The believers said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask your Lord to send it down upon them so that they believe." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: Say to those who believe: "And what makes you perceive that they will believe?" This is the reason for the accusative [fatḥa] in أنّ: "and what makes you perceive that they will believe", (and) We ﴿نُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾. Some read: (إنها) with kasra on the alif, (إذَا جَاءَتْ) as a fresh start, and make His saying (وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ) a self-sufficient statement. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: (وما يشعِركم إذا جاءتهم أنهم لا يؤمنون).
And (لا) in this place is a ṣila (redundant connective); like His saying: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: the meaning is: it is forbidden to them that they return. And similar to it: ﴿مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ لاَ تَسْجُدَ﴾, its meaning is: that you prostrate.
In the reading of Ubayy it is: (لعلها إِذا جاءتهم لا يؤمِنون). The Arabs have a usage for (لعلّ) in that they say: "ما أدرى أنك صاحبها" ("I do not know — perhaps you are the one"), meaning: لعلك صاحبها; and they say: "ما أدرى لو أنك صاحبها"; and it is a good interpretation to make (أنّ) stand in the place of لعل.

farraa:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ﴾: this is a thing they had asked for, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: if We did that for them they would not believe ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
His saying: (قُبُلاً) is the plural of qabīl, and al-qabīl is the guarantor (al-kafīl). I chose here that al-qubul should be in the sense of guaranteeing only because of their saying: ﴿أَوْ تَأتِى بِاللّهِ وَالْمَلاَئِكَةِ قَبِيلاً﴾ — guaranteeing that. And (قُبُلا) may mean: from before their faces; as you say: "I came to you from the front (قُبُلا) and did not come to you from behind (دُبُرا)". And al-qabīl may be a plural of qabīla (tribe), as though you said: or you bring us Allah and the angels tribe by tribe and group by group. And if it were read قَبَلا in the sense of "face to face (muʿāyanatan)" it would be correct, as you say: "أنا لقيته قبلا" ("I met him face to face").

farraa:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نِبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً شَيَاطِينَ ٱلإِنْسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ﴾: you put "enemy" and "devils" in the accusative by His saying: جعلنا.
His saying: ﴿يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾: Iblīs — according to what is mentioned — assigned one party of his devils to humans and one party to the jinn; when the devil of the human and the devil of the jinnī meet, [the first] says: "I led my companion astray with such and such, so lead your companion astray with it", and (the devil of the jinnī) says the like of that to him. This is their inspiring one another. Al-Farrāʾ said: Ḥayyān narrated that to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās.

farraa:113-113.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِيَقْتَرِفُواْ مَا هُم مُّقْتَرِفُونَ﴾: al-iqtirāf is earning; the Arabs say: "So-and-so went out to earn (yaqtarif) for his family."

farraa:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿مُنَزَّلٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾: of those who doubt that they know that it is sent down from your Lord.

farraa:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ in eating carrion, ﴿يُضِلُّوكَ﴾, because most of them were astray. That is because they said to the Muslims: "Do you eat what you have killed and not eat what your Lord has killed!" So this verse was sent down: ﴿وَإِن تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

farraa:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَن يَضِلُّ﴾: (من) is in the position of the nominative, like His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أىُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى﴾. When (من) comes after [verbs of] knowing, looking and perceiving — such as نظرت, علمت and دريت — it follows the pattern of أىّ. If after it there is a verb whose agent it is, you put it in the nominative by that verb; and if after it there is a verb that falls upon it, you put it in the accusative; as when you say: "ما أدرى من قام" ("I do not know who stood"), you put (من) in the nominative by قام; and "ما أدرى من ضربت" ("I do not know whom you struck"), you put it in the accusative by ضربت.

farraa:120-120.t: His saying: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ظَاهِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ﴾: as for its outward part, it is debauchery and fornication; and as for its inward part, it is secret companionship (al-mukhālla): that the woman takes a lover and that he takes her.

farraa:121-121.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ﴾: He says: your eating that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned is fisq, i.e. disbelief. He alluded to the eating [by the pronoun], as He said: ﴿فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَاناً﴾, meaning: the people's saying increased them in faith.

farraa:122-122.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَ مَن كَانَ مَيْتاً فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ﴾: i.e. he was astray and We guided him.
His saying: ﴿نُوراً يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ means his faith.

farraa:124-124.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُواْ صَغَارٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. from Allah; so said the exegetes. And in Arabic it is as you say: "سيأتينى رزق عندك" ("provision with you will come to me"), like your saying: "سيأتينى الذى عند الله" ("what is with Allah will come to me"): the humiliation that is with Him will strike them, and it is for Muhammad ﷺ to bring it down on them. But it is not permissible in Arabic to say "جئت عند زيد" while you mean "from Zayd (من عند زيد)".
And His saying ﴿صَغَارٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ may mean that they chose disbelief out of pride and disdain for following Muhammad ﷺ, so Allah made that humiliation in His sight.

farraa:125-125.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ﴾: [مَن] and مَن are in the position of the nominative by the hāʾ that refers back to each of them.
His saying: (يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرِجاً): Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿUmar read it (حرِجا), and the people read it حَرَجا. Al-ḥaraj — according to Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation — is a place thick with trees which the grazing flock cannot reach. He said: likewise the breast of the disbeliever, wisdom cannot reach it. With kasra and with fatḥa it is like waḥad and waḥid, farad and farid, danaf and danif: the Arabs say them with one meaning.
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾: He says: the way became narrow for him, and he found nothing but to climb into the sky, and he is not able. And it is read (كأنما يصَّاعَد), meaning يتصاعد, and (ويَصْعد) without doubling.

farraa:128-128.t: His saying: ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ﴾: He says: you have led many astray. His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ أَوْلِيَآؤُهُم مِّنَ ٱلإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا ٱسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنَا بِبَعْضٍ﴾: the humans' enjoyment of the jinn is that a man, when he went off alone and felt lonely, or killed one of their game and became afraid, would say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley", and would spend the night feeling safe. As for the jinn's enjoyment of humans, it is the reverence from humans that they obtained through them; the jinn used to say: "We have become lords of the jinn and the humans."

farraa:130-130.t:
His saying: ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ﴾: someone may say: the messengers are from humans only, so how did He say to the jinn and the humans (منكم) "from among you"? It is said: this is like His saying: ﴿مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ﴾, then He said: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾, whereas pearls and coral come out only from the salt water and not from the fresh.
So it is as though you said: they come out from part of them, from one of them.

farraa:131-131.t:
His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكَ أَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ رَّبُّكَ﴾: if you wish you may make (ذلك) in the position of the accusative, and make (أن) one of those where a genitive-governing preposition fits, so that when you drop it, it is accusative. He means: He did that because [your Lord] was not one to destroy the towns.
And if you wish you may make (ذلك) nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), since the verb is not overt. Similar to it: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾. And similar to it: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللّهُ مُوهِنُ كَيْد الْكَافِرِينَ﴾: the nominative and the accusative are permissible in all of it.
His saying: ﴿مُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا غَافِلُونَ﴾: He says: He was not one to destroy them for their wrongdoing while they are heedless, no messenger nor proof having yet come to them. And His saying in Hūd: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ الْقُرَى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ﴾: He says: He was not one to destroy them for their wrongdoing, i.e. for their associating partners [with Allah], (while their people are doing right), dealing with each other justly among themselves. Thus the exegesis has come. And there is another sense in it — and it is dearer to me than this, because associating partners [with Allah] is the greatest of sins — and the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: He was not one to destroy them by wrongdoing on His part while they are doing right.

farraa:99-99.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾: He says: the provision of every thing, meaning what grows and is fit as nourishment for every thing. Thus the exegesis has come, and it is the natural sense of the speech. In Arabic it is also permissible that you put "vegetation" in a genitive construct with "every thing" while by "every thing" you also mean the vegetation, so that it is like His saying: ﴿إنّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾, where al-yaqīn is the ḥaqq itself. His saying: ﴿مِنَ النَّخْلِ مِنْ طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ﴾: the proper form is the nominative for القنوان, because the meaning is: and from the palm trees, their clusters are near. If it were put in the accusative — "and He brought out from the palm trees, from their spathes, near clusters (قنوانا دانية)" — it would be permissible in speech, but it is not recited so because of the written text.
His saying: ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾ is accusative, except that the feminine plural with tāʾ takes the genitive ending in the position of the accusative; and if you put الجنات in the nominative following القنوان, it would be correct.
His saying: ﴿وَفِى الأَرضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ﴾: the proper form there is the nominative, making it follow القطع; and if you put it in the accusative and made it follow الرواسى and الأنهار, it would be correct.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ﴾ means the olive tree and the pomegranate trees, just as He said: ﴿وَاسْأَلَ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning the people of the town.
His saying: ﴿ٱنْظُرُوۤاْ إِلِىٰ ثَمَرِهِ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ﴾: He says: look at it when it first sets fruit, (وَيَنْعِهِ): its ripening. And it has been read (ويُنْعِهِ) and (ويانِعِهِ). As for His saying: ﴿ويُنْـعِهِ﴾, it is like "its ripeness (نضجه)", and يانعه is like "its ripe and mature state (ناضجه وبالغه)".

farraa:135-135.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ﴾: (مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ) is in the position of the nominative; and if you put it in the accusative it would be correct; as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَاللّهُ يَعْلَمُ المُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ﴾.
His saying: ﴿مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ﴾: when the subject of the verb is feminine and of the nature of a maṣdar (verbal noun), such as al-ʿāqiba (outcome), al-mawʿiẓa (admonition) and al-ʿāfiya (well-being), then when you put its verb before it you may make the verb feminine or masculine; as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَمَنْ جَاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ with the masculine, and said: ﴿قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ with the feminine. Likewise ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and ﴿وَأَخَذَتِ﴾. So do not shy away from either masculine or feminine in this.
[Translator's note: the source literally says "when the verb (al-fiʿl) is feminine"; al-Farrāʾ means the noun that the verb is predicated of.]

farraa:136-136.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا للَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ﴾, and برُعْمِهم and زِعمِهم: three dialect forms [Translator's note: the source writes برُعْمِهم with rāʾ, evidently for بزُعْمِهم]. No one we know of has read it with kasra on the zāy. The Arabs sometimes treat a word thus in cases like this; they say: al-fatk, al-futk and al-fitk, and al-wudd, al-widd and al-wadd, among similar words. The best of it is what the Readers from whom recitation is transmitted have chosen. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وهذا لشركائِهم"; and it is as you say in speech: ʿAbd Allāh said: "he has wealth (إنّ له مالا)" and "I have wealth (إنّ لى مالا)", meaning himself. And the poet said:
رَجْلانِ من ضَبّة أَخبرانا * إنا رأينا رجلا عريانا
(Two men of Ḍabba informed us: "We saw a naked man.")
And if he had said "they informed us that they had seen" it would be correct.

farraa:137-137.t:
His saying: ﴿ٰلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ﴾: they were a people who served their gods, and they made burying daughters alive seem fair to them. Also, one of them would say: "If such-and-such a number of males is born to me, I will sacrifice one of them." That is the killing of their children. And الشركاء is nominative, because they are the ones who made it seem fair.
Some used to read: "وكذلك زُيِّن لِكثِيرٍ مِن المشركين قتلُ أولادِهم", putting القتل in the nominative since its agent is not named, and putting (الشركاء) in the nominative by a verb he intends; as though he said: their partners made it seem fair to them. Similar to it is His saying: (يُسَبَّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالآصَالِ), then He said: ﴿رجَالٌ لاَ تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ﴾. In some of the codices of the people of Syria it is (شركايهم) with yāʾ; if that is established from the early ones, then it ought to be read (زُيِّنَ), and the partners would be the children, because they share with them in lineage and inheritance. But if they read (زَيَّنَ), I do not know its rationale; unless in it they were following the dialect of a people who say "أتيتها عِشايا" and then say in the dual of (الحمراء: حمرايان); this would be a way for them to have said: "زَيَّنَ لكثيرٍ من المشركين قتل أولادِهم شركايُهُمْ". And if you wish, when you read (زَيَّنَ) with fatḥa, you may make it a verb of Iblīs and then put الشركاء in the genitive as following الأولاد. The view of whoever said that they intended something like the poet's saying:
فزججتها متمكّنا * زجَّ القَلوصَ أبِى مزاد
(I thrust her firmly, as Abū Mazād thrusts the young she-camel.)
is worth nothing. This is among what the grammarians of the people of the Ḥijāz used to say, and we have not found its like in Arabic.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation is cut in the source as ﴿ٰلِكَ﴾, i.e. ﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ﴾; the poetic verse illustrates separating muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi by the object, the construction attributed to the Syrian reading زُيِّنَ … قتلُ أولادَهم شركائِهم.]

farraa:139-139.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is "خالص لذكورنا". Its being feminine is because of the femininity of الأنعام; since what is in their bellies is like them, it was made feminine because of their femininity. Whoever makes it masculine does so because (ما) is masculine. Some have read "خالصُهُ لذكورِنا", putting it in a genitive construct with the hāʾ, the hāʾ referring to ما. And you could put الخالص and الخالصة in the accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off), making the predicate of ما lie in the lām in His saying (لِذُكُورِنَا), as though you said: what is in the bellies of these cattle is for our males, exclusively (خالصا / خالصةً), as He said: ﴿وَلَهُ الدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾. But the accusative in this position is rare; they hardly say "عبدالله قائما فيها" ("ʿAbd Allāh, standing, is in it"), but it is analogically sound.
His saying: ﴿وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾: if you wish you may put الميتة in the nominative, and if you wish you may put it in the accusative, saying (ميتةً). And you may say تكن or يكن, with tāʾ or yāʾ.
And al-khāliṣa may be a maṣdar, given its feminine form, as you say al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya. It is like His saying: ﴿إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ﴾.

farraa:141-141.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ مَّعْرُوشَاتٍ وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشَاتٍ﴾: these are the vines. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُتَشَابِهاً﴾ in its colour, and ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ﴾ in its taste: some of it sweet and some of it sour.
His saying: ﴿وَآتُواْ حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ﴾: this is for the orphans and the poor who are present at it.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ﴾: in giving all of it. That is because Thābit ibn Qays left the people free to take from his palm trees, and all of it was taken and nothing of it remained for his family; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ إِنَّهُ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾.

farraa:142-142.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً﴾: He says: and He produced for you from the cattle beasts of burden (ḥamūla), meaning those able to carry and work; and al-farsh: the small ones.

farraa:143-143.t:
His saying: ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: if you wish you may make "eight" referred back (as badal) to الحمولة; and if you wish you may imply a verb for it.
His saying: ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: the male is a pair-member (zawj) and the female is a zawj. And if you put "two and two" in the nominative because of the entry of (مِن), it would be correct, as you say: "رأيت القوم منهم قاعد ومنهم قائم" ("I saw the people: of them is one sitting and of them one standing"), and [also] قاعد وقائما.
The meaning of His saying: ﴿قُلْ ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ﴾: He says: did the prohibition come to you, in what you have forbidden of the sāʾiba, the baḥīra, the waṣīla and the ḥām, from the two males or from the two females? If they said: "from the side of the male", every male would be forbidden to them; and if they said: "from the side of the female", every female would be forbidden to them.
Then He said: ﴿أَمَّا ٱشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ﴾: He says: or has He forbidden you what the womb contains? If they said that, male and female would be forbidden to them, because the womb contains both male and female. And (ما) in His saying "أمّا اشْتَمَلَتْ" is in the position of the accusative; you put it in the accusative as following the two males and the two females.

farraa:144-144.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ﴾: He says: did Allah enjoin this on you, you seeing it with your own eyes?

farraa:145-145.t:
His saying: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَجِدُ فِي مَآ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً﴾, then He, Majestic is His Face, said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً﴾; and if you wish, (تَكُونَ). In (الميتة) there are two possibilities: the nominative and the accusative. The nominative is not valid in recitation, because الدم is in the accusative by being referred back to الميتة, and it [i.e. أو دما] has an alif that prevents the nominative from being permissible. And (أن تكون) is permissible because الميتة is feminine, then you refer what comes after it back to it. Whoever puts (الميتة) in the nominative makes it the fiʿl of (يكون) [Translator's note: al-Farrāʾ's term; here: its subject], content with يكون without a predicate. Likewise (يكون) in all exception constructions does not need a predicate; do you not see that you say: "ذهب الناس إلا أن يكون أخاك" and "أخوك" ("the people went, unless it be your brother")? Kāna and yakūn could do without a predicate only as what follows إلا does without a verb belonging to the noun. Since it is said "قام الناس إلا زيدا" and "إلا زيد", putting it in the accusative without a verb and in the nominative without a verb, kāna was fit to be complete (tāmma).
Whoever reads the accusative says: kāna, by the Arabs' usage, has a nominative and an accusative, so they implied in kāna an unknown noun (ism majhūl) [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun of the matter, ḍamīr al-shaʾn], and made what comes after it the predicate (fiʿl) of that unknown. That is permissible with kāna, laysa and lam yazal, and with aẓunnu and its sisters: that you say (أظنه زيد أخوك, and) أظنّه فيها زيد ("I think — Zayd is in it"). And it is permissible with inna and its sisters; as in the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿يَا بُنَىّ إِنَّهَا إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ﴾, and as in His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ أَنَا اللّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾. You make the hāʾ masculine and singular; it is not permissible to make it dual, nor plural with a plural or anything else. Making it feminine with a feminine, and masculine with a feminine, is permissible; so you say: "إنها ذاهبة جاريتك" and "إنه ذاهبة جاريتك" ("your slave-girl is going").
If you say: how is the feminine permissible with the female, while the dual is not permissible with two? I say: because the Arabs only had regard to the feminine and masculine of the verb; since ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and ﴿وَأَخَذَتِ﴾ are permissible, feminine and masculine are permissible; and since "قاما أخواك" and "قاموا قومك" are not permissible, its dual and plural are not permissible.
If you say: do you permit its dual in the usage of those who say "ذهبا أخواك"? I say: no, because the verb is singular, and the alif in it is as it were an indication of the two doers of the verb, and the wāw in the plural indicates the doers of the verb; so it is not sound to allude to a verb and a noun in one knot. The verb is always singular, because the additions in it are nouns.
And you say, in two questions of this from which one may infer others: "إنها أسَد جاريتك" ("your slave-girl is a lion"), making it feminine because الأسد is the predicate (fiʿl) of الجارية; but if you made الجارية the predicate of الأسد and of masculine nouns like it, only the masculine hāʾ would be permissible. Likewise every masculine noun that you liken to a feminine, make the hāʾ masculine in it; and every feminine that you liken to a masculine, it has the hāʾ masculine or feminine; this is one. And whenever you make the verb of a feminine masculine, saying "قام جاريتك" or "طال صلاتك", (then introduce إنه on it), only the masculine is permissible, so you say: "إنه طال صلاتك" ("your prayer has become long"); you make it masculine because the verb is masculine; it is not permissible to make it feminine when the verb has been made masculine.
And when you see the noun put in the nominative by the locatives (al-maḥāll) — such as عندك, فوقك and فيها — use feminine or masculine with the feminine, and do not use the feminine with the masculine. That is because with the ṣifa (locative phrase) one cannot make it feminine as one can (in قام) جاريتك, by saying قامت جاريتك. Therefore with locative phrases the original form is followed.
And when you devote kāna to a single noun, you may put it in the nominative and make the verb belong to it. And if you wish, you may imply in it an unknown [noun] and put what comes after it in the accusative, saying: "إذا كان غدا فأتنا" ("when it is tomorrow, come to us"). And you say: "اذهب فليس إلا أباك" and "أبوك" ("go, for there is none but your father"). Whoever reads the nominative implies "anyone", as though he said: there is no one but your father; and whoever reads the accusative implies the unknown noun and puts it in the accusative; because the unknown is definite, therefore you put it in the accusative. And whoever says "إذا كان غُدْوةً فأتنا" ("when it is morning, come to us") may not say "إذا غدوةً كان فأتنا"; likewise the unknown noun may not be preceded by its accusative. And when you couple an indefinite noun with a locative phrase (ṣifa) in kāna, saying "إن كان بينهم شرّ فلا تقربهم" ("if there is evil between them, do not approach them"), you put it in the nominative. And if you begin with الشر and put the locative phrase after it, the proper form is the nominative, saying: "إن شر بينهم فلا تقربهم", and the accusative is permissible. He said: and one of them recited to me:
فعينَىَّ هلاَّ تبكيان عِفَاقا * إذا كان طعنا بينهم وعِناقا
(O my two eyes, will you not weep for ʿIfāq, when there was spearing between them and close grappling?)
When you devote kāna to an indefinite noun alone, the accusative and nominative are equal; and when you devote kāna to a definite noun alone, the proper form is the accusative; they say: "لو كان إلا ظله لخاب ظله" ("if it were [nothing] but his shadow, his shadow would fail"). These are as I have described to you.

farraa:146-146.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَآ﴾: He forbade them the omentum (al-tharb) and the fat of the kidneys.
Then He said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا﴾: and (ما) is in the position of the accusative by the verb, through the exception.
And (الحَوَايَا) is in the position of the nominative, referring it back to الظهور: "except what their backs carry or the entrails carry"; and they are the intestines and the "daughters of milk" (bināt al-laban). The accusative is on your intending (أو شحوم الحوايا) "or the fat of the entrails", dropping "fat" and contenting yourself with "entrails"; as He said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning: and ask the people of the town.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ﴾: it is the fat-tail (al-alya). And (ما) is in the position of the accusative.

farraa:151-151.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْاْ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْئاً﴾: if you wish you may make (لاَ تُشْرِكُوا) a prohibition on which you have brought in (أن); and if you wish you may make it a statement (khabar), with (تشِركوا) in the position of the accusative; as when you say: "أمرتك ألاَّ تذهبَ إلى زيد" ("I commanded you not to go to Zayd") (accusative), and "أن لا تذهبْ" (jussive). And if you wish you may make what you have joined on to (أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُوا بِه) partly jussive and partly accusative; as He said: ﴿قُلْ إِنِّى أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ﴾: He put the first of it in the accusative and prohibited in the last of it; as the poet said:
حجَّ وأوصى بسليمى الأعبدا * ألاّ ترى ولا تكلمْ أحدا * ولا تُمَشِّ بفَضاء بعدَا
(He went on pilgrimage and charged the slaves concerning Sulaymā: that she should see no one, and "speak to no one, and do not walk in open country afterwards".)
He intended a statement in its first part and a prohibition in its last. He said: and the jussive in this verse is dearer to me because of His saying: (وَأَوفُوا الْكَيْلَ); so I made its first part a prohibition because of His saying: (وَأَوفُوا الْكَيْلَ).

farraa:153-153.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ هَـٰذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيماً﴾: you put kasra on إنّ when you intend a resumption (istiʾnāf), and fatḥa because (أتل) falls on it. And if you wish you may make it genitive, meaning ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ﴾ and [by] ﴿وَأَنَّ هَـٰذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيماً فَٱتَّبِعُوهُ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلسُّبُلَ﴾ means Judaism and Christianity. He says: do not follow them, or you will go astray.

farraa:154-154.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ تَمَاماً عَلَى ٱلَّذِيۤ أَحْسَنَ﴾: as a completion for the one who does good. And "the one who does good" may have the sense of a plural; as He said: ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (تَمَاماً عَلَى الذِين أحسنوا), confirming that.
And if you wish you may make (الذى) in the sense of (ما), meaning: as a completion for what Moses did well, so that the meaning is: as a completion for his good-doing. And (أحسن) may be nominative, meaning: for the one who is best [i.e. الذى هو أحسنُ]; and you put (أحسن) in the accusative [form] here while intending the genitive by it; because the Arabs say: "مررت بالذى هوخير منك وشر منك" ("I passed by the one who is better than you, and worse than you"), but they do not say "مررت بالذى قائم"; because "خيرا منك" is like a definite noun, since alif and lām do not enter it. Likewise they say: "مررت بالذى أخيك" and "بالذى مثلِك" ("by the one who is your brother", "by the one who is like you"); when they make the ṣila (relative clause) of الذى a definite noun, or an indefinite noun that alif and lām do not enter, they make it follow الذى [in case]. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
إن الزُّبيرىَّ الذى مِثْلَ الحَلَمْ * مَشَّى بأسلابك فى أهل العَلَم
(The Zubayrid, the one who is like a tick, paraded your spoils among the people of the banner.)

farraa:155-155.t: His saying: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ﴾: you have made "blessed" a naʿt (adjective) of the Book, so you put it in the nominative. If you put it in the accusative, as departing from the hāʾ in (أَنْزَلْنَاهُ) [i.e. as a ḥāl], it would be correct.

farraa:156-156.t: His saying: ﴿أَن تَقُولُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَابُ﴾: (أن) is in the position of the accusative from two directions. One of them: We sent it down lest you say: "it was only sent down…". The other is from His saying: "and beware lest you say". (لا) is fit in the place of (أن) here, like His saying: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾, in which (لا تضلون) is fit; as He said: ﴿سَلَكْنَاهُ فِى قُلُوبِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ. لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾.

farraa:158-158.t: His saying: ﴿ هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيهُمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾: to take their souls; ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ﴾: the Resurrection; ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ آيَاتِ رَبِّكَ﴾: the rising of the sun from its place of setting.

farraa:159-159.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمْ﴾: ʿAlī read it (فارقوا), and said: "By Allah, they did not divide it, but they abandoned it." They are the Jews and the Christians. The people read it (فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ), and each is a valid reading.
His saying: ﴿لَّسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ﴾: He says: you have nothing to do with fighting them; then it was abrogated by: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ﴾.

farraa:160-160.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا﴾: whoever reads the genitive means: he will have ten good deeds like it. And if He had said here "فله عشر مِثْلِها", meaning ten good deeds like it, it would be correct. Whoever says "عشْرٌ أَمثالها" makes them a naʿt (adjective) of the ten. And (مثل) may be singular: you say in speech of this kind "هم مثلكم" and "أمثالكم" ("they are like you"); Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿إِنكم إِذاً مثلهم﴾, using the singular, and said: ﴿ثم لا يكونوا أَمثالكم﴾, using the plural. And if you said "عَشْرٌ أمثالها", as you say "عندى خمسةٌ أثوابٌ" ("I have five garments"), it would be permissible.
His saying: ﴿مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ﴾: with "there is no god but Allah"; and the evil deed: associating partners [with Allah].

farraa:161-161.t: His saying: ﴿دِيناً قِيَماً﴾ and "قَيِّما". Muḥammad narrated to us, he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated to me from a man from ʿImrān ibn Ḥudhayfa, he said: My father Ḥudhayfa saw me bowing with my head lowered; he said: "Raise your head — an upright religion (دينا قيما)." (دينا قيما) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and (مِلةَ إِبراهِيم) likewise.

farraa:165-165.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلاَئِفَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: the community of Muhammad ﷺ was made the successors of all the nations; ﴿ورفع بعضكم فوق بعضٍ درجاتٍ﴾ in provision, (لِيبلوكم) by that (فِيما آتاكم).

farraa:6-6.t: His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ﴾ — a qarn (generation) is eighty years; some have said: seventy.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ﴾ — if you wish, you can make (الرحمة) the end of a statement and then begin afresh after it with (ليَجْمَعَنَّكم). And if you wish, you can treat it [the following clause] as being in the position of the accusative, as He said: ﴿كَتَب ربكم على نفسِهِ الرحمة أَنه من عمل مِنكم﴾. With the words that admit the answer of an oath, the Arabs use both «أن» with fatḥa and the lām. So they say: "arsaltu ilayhi an yaqūma" ("I sent to him that he should stand"), and "arsaltu ilayhi la-yaqūmanna" ("I sent to him [saying] he shall surely stand").
Likewise His saying: ﴿ثم بدا لهم مِن بعدِ ما رأَوُا الآياتِ ليسجُنُنَّهُ﴾, and this is frequent in the Qurʾān. Do you not see that if you said "badā lahum an yasjunūhu" ("it occurred to them to imprison him"), it would be correct?

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَتَّخِذُ وَلِيّاً فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ — [«فاطر»] is genitive in its case: you make it one of the attributes of Allah, Blessed and Exalted. Had you put it in the accusative as praise, it would have been correct, since it is definite. And had you intended "fāṭiran" in the sense of "creator" [i.e. as an indefinite participle], you would put it in the accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off), since it has no alif-lām. Had you begun afresh and put it in the nominative, it would have been correct, as He said: (ربُّ السمواتِ والأَرضِ وما بينهما الرحمن).

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ﴾ — everything that subdues something is above it.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿لأُنذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَن بَلَغَ﴾ — He means: and whomever the Qurʾān reaches after you. (بلغ) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من), and (من) is put in the accusative by the warning.
His saying: ﴿آلِهَةً أُخْرَىٰ﴾ — He did not say "ukhar" (plural), because «الآلهة» is a plural, and (a plural) can be treated as feminine [singular], as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿ولِلّهِ الأَسماءُ الحسنى﴾, and Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿فما بال القُرونِ الأُولى﴾, and did not say "al-uwal" or "al-awwalīn". All of that is correct.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَآءَهُمُ﴾ — it is mentioned that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: "What is this recognition by which you recognise Muhammad ﷺ?" He said: "By Allah, when I see him I know him better than I know my own son while he is playing with the boys; for I have no doubt about him that he is Muhammad ﷺ, whereas I do not know what the women may have done regarding the son." So this recognition is by his description in their Book.
The exegesis has come concerning His saying: ﴿خَسِرُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ — it is said: there is no believer and no unbeliever but he has a dwelling in Paradise, and a family and spouses. Whoever embraces Islam and is felicitous goes to his dwelling and his spouses, (and whoever disbelieves, his dwelling and his spouses go) to the one who embraced Islam and was felicitous. That is His saying ﴿الذِين يَرِثُون الفِردوسَ﴾ — He is saying: they inherit the dwellings of the unbelievers; and that is His saying: ﴿الذِين خسِروا أنفسهم وأهليهم﴾.

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾ — it is read «ربِّنَا» and «ربَّنا», in the genitive and the accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh, the brother of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, related to me from al-Aʿmash, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAlqama, that he read (واللّهِ ربَّنا), and said: its meaning is "By Allah, O our Lord." Whoever says (ربِّنا) makes it [part of] what is sworn by.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَلدَّارُ ٱلآخِرَةُ﴾ — «الدار» is made a noun here and «الآخرة» is made its description, while in other places it is put in a construct [«دار الآخرة»]. Similar to it, among things annexed to what is like them in meaning, is His saying ﴿إِنّ هذا لهو حَقُّ اليَقِين﴾: "the truth" is "the certainty", just as "the abode" is "the hereafter". Likewise "I came to you bāriḥata al-ūlā" and "al-bāriḥata al-ūlā" ("the night before last"). And of it is "yawm al-khamīs" ("the day of Thursday") and "laylat al-khamīs". A thing is annexed to itself when its wording differs, just as «الحق» and «اليقين», «الدار» and «الآخرة», and «اليوم» and «الخميس» differ.
When they agree, the Arabs do not say "ḥaqq al-ḥaqq" or "yaqīn al-yaqīn", because when the two differ in wording they fancy that they differ in meaning. Similar to it is, in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, (وذلك الدِين القَيِّمة), and in our reading (دِين القَيِّمة). Al-qayyim and al-qayyima are like your saying "a man who is a rāwiya (great transmitter) and a wahhāba (great giver) of wealth", alongside wahhāb and rāwin, and the like.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾ — the generality read it with the doubled form. He said: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ al-Asadī related to me from Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, from Nājiya ibn Kaʿb, from ʿAlī, that he read (يُكْذِبونك), in the light form.
The meaning of the light form — and Allah knows best — is: they do not make you out to be a liar; they only mean that what you have brought is false. For they had never found him ﷺ to lie, so as to call him a liar (yukadhdhibūhu); rather they declared [what he brought] false (akdhabūhu), i.e. what you have brought is a lie that we do not recognise. Takdhīb is to say: "You have lied." And Allah knows best.

farraa:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِن ٱسْتَطَعْتَ أَن تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَأْتِيَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ﴾ — "then do so" is implied; thus the exegesis has come, and that is its meaning. The Arabs do this only in every place where the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb) is known. Do you not see that you say to a man "If you are able to give charity…", "If you see fit to stand with us…", leaving out the apodosis, because you know that he knows it? But when there comes something whose apodosis is known only by its being expressed, you express it, as in your saying to a man: "If you stand, you will obtain good." In this there must be an apodosis, because its meaning is not known if it is dropped.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ﴾ — (الطائر) is genitive. Its nominative is permissible, (as you say: "mā ʿindī min) rajulin wa-lā imraʾatin" and "imraʾatun"; whoever uses the nominative means: "I have no man, and I have no woman." Likewise His saying: ﴿وما يعزُبُ عن ربِّك مِن مِثقالِ ذرةٍ﴾, after which He said (ولا أصغرَ مِن ذلك، ولا أَصغرُ ولا أَكبرَ، ولا أَكبرُ): if you put (أصغر) in the accusative [form], it is intended as genitive [being a diptote]; and whoever uses the nominative refers it back to the meaning.
As for His saying ﴿وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ﴾: a bird flies only with its two wings. In speech it is like His saying (له تِسع وتسعون نعجة [ولى نعجة] أنثى), and like your saying to a man: "I spoke to him with my own mouth," and "I walked to him on my own feet," for emphasis in speech.
It is said that every kind of animal is a community (umma). The Arabs say ṣinf [and ṣanf] (kind).
﴿ثم إِلى ربِّهِم يحشرون﴾ — their gathering is their death; then they are gathered with mankind and are told: "Be dust!" At that point the unbeliever wishes that he were dust like them.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُكُم﴾ — the Arabs have two usages and two meanings in (أرأيت).
One of them is that a man asks another: "Have you seen Zayd with your own eyes?" This is with the hamza. If you apply it to the man himself, you say: "a-raʾaytaka ʿalā ghayri hādhihi al-ḥāl?", meaning: "Have you seen yourself in a state other than this?" Then you make it dual and plural, saying to two men "a-raʾaytumākumā", to a group "a-raʾaytumūkum", to women "a-raʾaytunnakunna", and to a woman "a-raʾaytiki", with kasra on the tāʾ and the kāf; nothing but that is permissible.
The other meaning is that you say "a-raʾaytaka" meaning "Tell me" (and you pronounce it with hamza), giving the tāʾ fatḥa; or you leave out the hamza if you wish, which is most of the speech of the Arabs. And you leave the tāʾ singular with fatḥa for the masculine and feminine singular [and the plural, in] its feminine and masculine. So you say to a woman: "a-raʾaytaki Zaydan hal kharaja?" ("Tell me, has Zayd gone out?"), and to women: "a-raʾaytakunna Zaydan mā faʿala?" ("Tell me, what has Zayd done?"). The Arabs left the tāʾ singular only because they did not intend the action from it to fall upon the person himself; so they were content to mark the person in the kāf, and they directed the tāʾ toward the masculine and the singular, since the action did not fall [on an object]. The position of the kāf is accusative, but its interpretation is nominative; just as when you say to a man "dūnaka Zaydan" ("Take Zayd!"), you find the kāf genitive in wording but nominative in meaning, because it is the one commanded.
When the Arabs make the action of something fall upon itself, with the noun referred to by a pronoun, they say with the complete verbs something other than what they say with the deficient (nāqiṣa) ones. To a man one says: "You killed yourself (nafsaka)" and "You did good to yourself (nafsika)"; they do not say "qataltaka" or "aḥsanta ilayka". Thus Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿فاقتلوا أنفسكم﴾, as in much of the Qurʾān, like His saying ﴿وماظلمناهم ولكِن ظلموا أنفسهم﴾. But when the verb is deficient — like ḥasibtu and ẓanantu — they say: "aẓunnunī khārijan" ("I think myself to be going out"), "aḥsibunī khārijan", and "matā tarāka khārijan?" ("When do you see yourself going out?"); and they do not say "matā tarā nafsaka" or "matā taẓunnu nafsaka". That is because they wanted to distinguish between the verb that may be suspended (yulghā) and the verb whose suspension is not permissible. Do you not see that you say "anā — aẓunnu — khārijun" ("I am — I think — going out"), cancelling (أظنّ), so that the noun's own operator governs it? [Translator's note: «العفل» in the text is evidently a misprint for «الفعل».]
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has said ﴿إِن الإِنسان ليطغى. أَن رآه استغنى﴾, and did not say "raʾā nafsahu". In poetry "ḍarabtaka" or the like may occur with a complete verb. Of that is the poet's saying:
خُذَا حَذراً يا جارتىَّ فإننى * رأيتُ جِرَان العَوْدِ قد كاد يُصْلح
لقد كان لى فى ضَرّتين عدِمتُنى * وما كنت أَلقَى من رزينة أَبرحُ
(Take care, my two wives, for I have seen that the neck-hide of the old camel [i.e. the whip] is nearly ready. I had, in two co-wives — may I lose myself! — and in what I used to suffer from Razīna, more than enough distress.)
The Arabs say "ʿadimtunī" ("may I lose myself"), "wajadtunī" and "faqadtunī", but it is not the proper form of speech.

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاۤ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا تَضَرَّعُواْ﴾ — the meaning of (فلولا) is "why not then" (fa-hallā). It can also have the meaning of «لولا» [counterfactual], as though you said: "Were it not for ʿAbd Allāh, I would strike you." If you see after it a single noun in the nominative, it is in the sense of the «لولا» whose apodosis has the lām; and if you do not see a noun after it, it is a question [an incitement], as in His saying: ﴿لولا أَخَّرْتَنِى إلى أَجلٍ قريب [فأصدّق وأَكُن مِنَ الصالِحِين]﴾ and His saying: ﴿فلولا إِن كنتم غير مدِينين [ترجِعونها إن كنتّم صادِقِين]﴾. Likewise (لوما) has in it what is in «لولا»: the question and the statement.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوَابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ — He means the gates of provision and rain, which is the good things of this world, in order to try them by it. It is like His saying: ﴿حتى إذا أخَذَتِ الأَرْضُ زُخْرُفها وازَّيَّنَتْ وظنّ أَهْلُها أنهم قادِرون عليها أتاها أَمْرُنا ليلا أَوْ نهارا﴾, and similar is ﴿وأن لوِ استقاموا على الطرِيقةِ لأسقيناهم ماءً غدَقا لِنفتِنهم فيه﴾ — the "way" is the way of shirk; i.e. had they persisted in it, We would have done that to them.
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ مُّبْلِسُونَ﴾ — al-mublis is one who despairs, whose hope has been cut off. That is why it is said of someone who falls silent when his argument fails and he has no answer: "He has become mublis (ablasa)." The rajaz poet said:
يا صاحِ هل تعرف رَسْما مُكْرَسَا * قال نعم أعرِفه، وأبلسا
(O companion, do you recognise a trace [of an encampment] covered with dung? He said: Yes, I recognise it — and fell silent.)
i.e. he gave me no answer.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾ — [the pronoun] refers to the loss of hearing and sight and the sealing of hearts. When you refer to actions, even if they are many, you make the pronoun singular, as in your saying to a man: "Your coming and your going annoy (yuʾdhīnī) me." It is also said that the hāʾ in (به) refers to guidance; and it is like the first interpretation.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنذِرْ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَن يُحْشَرُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — He is saying: they fear being gathered to their Lord, knowing that it will happen. That is why the exegetes explained (يخافون) as "they know".

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾ — someone may ask: how would the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drive away anyone who calls upon his Lord, so that he should be forbidden that? It has reached us that ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī came in to the Prophet ﷺ while Salmān, Bilāl, Ṣuhayb and their like were with him. ʿUyayna said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you were to put these away from you, the nobles of your people would come to you and embrace Islam." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِٱلْغَدَاةِ وَٱلْعَشِيِّ﴾.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكاً لَّجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلاً﴾ — in the form of a man, because they are not able to look upon the form of an angel.
